findings.title: GithubClaimLease >100-Comment Pagination Truncation Race
findings.invariant: Mutual exclusion: at most one factory worker acquires the exclusive claim lease on an issue.
findings.severity_rationale: Directly breaks single-holder authority. When an issue has >100 comments, two concurrent claimants beyond comment 100 both return ClaimResult.Acquired, creating active split-brain execution on the same task.
findings.description: GithubClaimLease.listComments queries /issues/{n}/comments?per_page=100 without handling Link headers or subsequent pages. When comment count exceeds 100, page 1 comments (1..100) fill the buffer. Boundary markers and competing claims on page 2+ are completely unseen by listComments. GithubClaimWindow parses only page 1, and for both racing claimants on page 2+, winnerAgainst(ownCommentId) returns Optional.empty(). Both claimants fall back to winnerId = ownCommentId and return ClaimResult.Acquired. Confirmed by physical WireMock reproducer.

findings.title: BestEffortPush Non-Fast-Forward Rejection is Remote Protection Only, Not a Local Fence
findings.invariant: Fail-closed fencing: a superseded or zombie worker must not advance round persistence when its push is rejected.
findings.severity_rationale: ADR 0002 documents git non-fast-forward push rejection as a hard zombie fence. In code, push rejection is swallowed as a WARN and does not throw, delegating the entire fence to post-persist tracker checks.
findings.description: BestEffortPush.pushBestEffort is void; on a nonzero push command result it calls PushOutcome.describe("push", result), logs WARN OperatorEvent.PUSH_FAILED when outcome text is non-null, then returns normally without throwing. GitAttemptPersistence treats local commit creation as the durability boundary. Consequently, round persistence succeeds locally and proceeds to RevocationCheckingAttemptPersistence, rather than terminating immediately.

findings.title: Truncation-Assisted Zombie Fence Defeat and Divergent Local Round Execution
findings.invariant: Zombie execution termination: a superseded worker must halt when checked against tracker authority.
findings.severity_rationale: Combines GNOMISH-CLAIM-01 and GNOMISH-FENCE-01. When comment count exceeds 100, the tracker check fails to detect revocation, allowing the zombie worker to execute subsequent rounds locally and perform uncoordinated actions.
findings.description: ZombieFenceSpec asserts that a zombie worker halts because tracker.fetchTask() returns Working(NEW_HOLDER). However, on GitHub tracker implementation, GithubTaskFetcher queries /comments?per_page=100. If instance A was reaped and instance B claimed at comment 102: when zombie instance A calls fetchTask(), it receives page 1 (comments 1..100) where instance A appears as the latest claim. fetchTask() returns Working('instance-A')! RevocationCheckingAttemptPersistence checks holder.equals(instanceId) which evaluates to TRUE. Because BestEffortPush swallowed the push failure and returned normally, zombie instance A continues executing subsequent rounds locally, producing diverging local commits.

findings.title: Heartbeat and Reaper Blinding via Comment Truncation
findings.invariant: Tracker authority convergence: heartbeat renewal and stale claim removal must observe active tenures.
findings.severity_rationale: Causes healthy workers to self-fence prematurely due to false ClaimGone detection, while blinding the reaper from observing newer claims beyond comment 100.
findings.description: GithubHeartbeat.resolveClaim and GithubStaleClaimRemoval.reReadThread both execute GET /issues/{num}/comments?per_page=100 without pagination. If the active claim comment was posted at index >= 101, resolveClaim returns Optional.empty(), causing GithubHeartbeat to return BeatResult.Lost(ClaimGone). A healthy live worker immediately self-fences. Conversely, the reaper reReadThread inspects obsolete page 1 data and fails to observe newer claims or boundaries.

findings.title: JudgeVerdictExtractor Pass Smuggling via Preliminary Code Fence
findings.invariant: Verification soundness: stage evaluation must reflect the judge model's terminal verdict, not preliminary text.
findings.severity_rationale: Allows failing code to advance into delivery. A model discussing test examples or mock configs with {"passed": true} causes the extractor to emit Pass, completely ignoring a terminal Fail verdict.
findings.description: JudgePromptBuilder asks the judge model to end its message with a JSON verdict object. However, JudgeVerdictExtractor uses FENCE.matcher(text).find() to match the FIRST markdown code fence and scans for the FIRST balanced JSON object from the start. If the judge quotes a test case, mock configuration, or preliminary reasoning containing {"passed": true} before its terminal verdict, the extractor extracts the preliminary fence and returns Verdict.Pass(), discarding terminal failure findings. Confirmed by physical Spock court.

findings.title: Non-JSON Code Fence Preceding Verdict Induces Premature CannotVerify Escalation
findings.invariant: Evaluation determinism: code formatting in explanations must not corrupt stage attempt accounting.
findings.severity_rationale: Causes premature human escalation without burning stage retry attempts when the judge includes code examples.
findings.description: When a judge model quotes illustrative code (Java/Python/Bash) with braces prior to its JSON verdict fence, JudgeVerdictExtractor attempts to parse that first fence as JSON. Parsing fails and returns Verdict.CannotVerify. In JudgeVoting, a single CannotVerify vote short-circuits the voting loop and marks the check CannotVerify, which StageAttemptLoop treats as an unburned infrastructure failure, triggering human escalation without consuming attempt budgets.

findings.name: Judge Tool-Permission Argv Collapse on Empty Read-Only Intersection
findings.invariant: Least privilege: judge agents must run with strictly read-only tools.
findings.severity_rationale: Policy/argv collapse physically proven: when manifest contains only write tools or empty list, the --allowedTools restriction is omitted from argv.
findings.description: AgentInvocationOptions.renderForJudge filters manifest allowedTools against JUDGE_READ_ONLY_TOOLS (['Read', 'Grep', 'Glob']). When the intersection is empty (e.g. stage requested only ['Write', 'Bash'] or []), effectiveJudgeAllowedTools returns []. addToolListFlag omits the --allowedTools flag entirely when the list is empty, generating argv containing only ['--model', '<model>']. Evidence boundary: while argv omission is physically confirmed by JudgeVerificationCourt, live network test against provider is bounded by Teamwork anti-recursion policy; whether print mode defaults to unprompted writes or rejects tools is unverified at runtime.

findings.title: Shared Container Instance Reuse Across Attempt Judge Votes
findings.invariant: Voter independence: judge votes must evaluate attempts in independent, uncontaminated environments.
findings.severity_rationale: Reuses the exact same container across multiple votes for the same attempt commit SHA. If combined with tool leakage, earlier votes contaminate later votes.
findings.description: FreshJudgeEnvironments caches and reuses the same TaskExecutionEnvironment instance across all votes for an attempt commit SHA. The architectural justification assumed judges are strictly read-only. If GNOMISH-JUDGE-03 omits tool restrictions, an earlier voter that performs filesystem writes mutates the environment for subsequent voters, undermining voting independence.

findings.title: Egress Guard Permissive Host Routing to Endpoints on Allowlisted Domains
findings.invariant: Data loss prevention: sandboxed processes must not exfiltrate source code or credentials.
findings.severity_rationale: Shipped core enforces only L4/SNI hostname allowlisting without TLS inspection. Hostname allowlisting permits the network path to arbitrary endpoints on that host.
findings.description: Shipped core egress guard uses mitmdump strictly at L4/SNI/CONNECT level with data.ignore_connection = True (no TLS termination or path inspection). When a domain such as github.com is allowlisted, the network path to any endpoint on that host is open; successful exfiltration or write operations (e.g. git push to an external repository or posting to an issue/gist) depend on attacker-available or foreign credentials, or unauthenticated writable endpoints. Crucial distinction: L7 path/verb enforcement, TLS re-signing, and local AI gateway credential scrubbing are proposed future hardenings (add-sandbox-hardening, Change B), NOT shipped in the current core codebase.

findings.title: Host Escape and Docker Daemon Socket Access
findings.invariant: Host isolation: in-box container processes must not access host sockets, host filesystems, or escape namespace boundaries.
findings.severity_rationale: Hypothesis that containers can access host sockets or escape volumes was physically disproved by code inspection and existing test suite.
findings.description: Task containers mount exclusively a single per-task named volume (/gnomish/work). No host filesystems or sockets (/var/run/docker.sock) are mounted. Container file channel normalizes paths lexically and forbids traversal outside workingCopy or scratch, blocking .git/**. Anonymous image volumes are replaced with ephemeral tmpfs, and EnvironmentSelfCheck enforces non-root execution (UID 1000) and internal network configuration fail-closed.

findings.title: Remote Git History Overwrite via Zombie Force-Push
findings.invariant: Remote branch immutability: a superseded zombie worker must not overwrite remote git history.
findings.severity_rationale: Hypothesis that a zombie worker could overwrite remote history via forced pushes was physically disproved.
findings.description: Git commands in the codebase never supply --force or +refspec. NoForcePushGuardSpec scans all git command builders at compile time. Git remote origin rejects non-fast-forward pushes. Remote git branch truth remains protected from destruction even when local round execution diverges.
